text:
Bedding supplies after closing stayed on our minds, and we value your kind words. You said the companion animal service felt disorganized at the gate, that the handoff of bedding was missed after closing, and that this left you worried about your pet's comfort. I am sorry for that experience, and I want to address it clearly from the Companion Animal Travel Desk.

Our desk team is expected to log every service change in the desk ledger before a flight leaves our care. That record is what helps the crew know which supplies need to follow the animal, which carrier notes need extra attention, and which comfort items should be checked again before boarding ends. When a bedding request is not carried through, the right response is not to shrug it off, but to review the handoff, correct the record, and make sure the crew receives the practical instructions they need.

For future travel, please let the check-in agent know right away if your pet needs bedding, a quieter placement, or a more careful comfort plan. Our care plans account for species, temperament, and comfort, so the more detail we have, the better we can match the setup to the animal. If your companion is anxious, older, or sensitive to movement, tell us that too. Small notes can change how the team prepares the space.

I have also asked the shift staff to recheck the storage flow for post-close supplies and to keep the ledger entries plain and complete. That helps us avoid missed items and gives the crew a cleaner path to follow. If you travel with us again, we will be ready to use that information and keep the process steadier from desk to cabin.

Thank you for taking the time to write in. Your message helps us improve a routine that should be calm, careful, and reliable for both travelers and their animals.

Companion Animal Travel Desk
